items: Map Your Child's Food Landscape: Create a Traffic Light document with Green, Yellow, and Red food columns to categorize exactly what your child eats reliably, conditionally, and refuses across all settings.

Map Your Child's Food Landscape: Identify every caregiver who feeds your child and document each person's current feeding behaviors and rules so you know precisely where inconsistency exists in your system.
Map Your Child's Food Landscape: Track which foods your child requests from specific caregivers versus which foods they refuse from you to reveal where strategic behavior patterns have developed.
Map Your Child's Food Landscape: Distinguish between foods your child genuinely dislikes versus foods they refuse because they know different caregivers have different rules about what gets offered.

Align All Caregivers on the System: Schedule a direct conversation with every caregiver who feeds your child and explain that your feeding approach is based on research showing inconsistent rules make selective eating worse, not better.

Align All Caregivers on the System: Create a written feeding agreement that specifies exactly which foods will be offered, which short-order options are off-limits, and what alternatives are acceptable when your child refuses.

Align All Caregivers on the System: Establish consistent language and responses that every caregiver will use when your child protests so your child encounters the same messages about food in every setting.

Align All Caregivers on the System: Set up a daily communication system between caregivers to share what was eaten, what was refused, and any incidents where the rules were broken so problems get addressed quickly.

Implement Daily Consistency: Commit to never short-order cooking or making separate meals when your child refuses what is offered, because one exception teaches your child that persistence produces results.

Implement Daily Consistency: Plan weekly menus that always include at least one Green food your child reliably eats alongside Yellow foods being targeted for expansion so your child has a safety net at every meal.

Implement Daily Consistency: Address grandparent resistance by explaining that short-term accommodation solves their discomfort but deepens your child's problem by teaching her that the rules are not real.

Implement Daily Consistency: Review caregiver alignment weekly and reinforce commitments, because school-age children test boundaries constantly and caregivers need ongoing reminders about why consistency matters.
